title: Fixed #37357 -- Handled out-of-range year in admin date_hierarchy.
body:
#### Trac ticket number

ticket-37357

#### Branch description

`ChangeList.get_filters()` catches only `ValueError` around the `datetime(...)`
construction in the admin `date_hierarchy` handling, while the `to_date`
computation sits outside the `try`. An out-of-range year query parameter
therefore escapes as an unhandled exception (HTTP 500) instead of the intended
`IncorrectLookupParameters` (which the changelist view turns into a redirect to
`?e=1`):

- `?<datefield>__year=9999` — `datetime(9999, 1, 1)` succeeds, then
  `to_date = from_date.replace(year=from_date.year + 1)` raises
  `ValueError: year 10000 is out of range` (outside the `try`).
- `?<datefield>__year=99999999999999999999` — `datetime(...)` raises
  `OverflowError`, which `except ValueError` does not catch.

Any authenticated staff user with view permission on a model whose admin sets
`date_hierarchy` (a common configuration) can trigger it. This change catches
`(ValueError, OverflowError)` and moves the `to_date` computation inside the
`try`, matching the handling Django already uses for this int-to-datetime
parsing pattern in `views/generic/dates.py`, `views/static.py`,
`template/defaultfilters.py`, and `contrib/auth/views.py`. A regression test is
added in `tests/admin_changelist`.

#### AI Assistance Disclosure (REQUIRED)
- [ ] **No AI tools were used** in preparing this PR.
- [x] **If AI tools were used**, I have disclosed which ones, and fully reviewed and verified their output.

AI tool used: Claude Code (Anthropic). It assisted in locating the issue and
drafting the fix and regression test; the output was reviewed and verified
locally — the new test fails before the change and passes after, and the full
`admin_changelist` suite passes (106 tests).
